### *Chaeropus ecaudatus*
### Blamed on foxes

::::

<center>
IUCN status: **Extinct**

Last seen: *Chaeropus ecaudatus were last seen in 1901 in Alice Springs, NT (IUCN 2023)*

IUCN claim: *"The extinction of the Pig-footed Bandicoot is attributed to predation by feral cats and red foxes."*

</center>


### Studies in support

No studies

### Studies not in support

Southern pig-footed bandicoots were last confirmed in the Murray-Darling, Alice Springs, Western Division of NSW, Youndegin, and southwest Australia 49-23, 19-14, 30-5, 32-27, and 95-61 years before foxes arrived, respectively (Wallach et al. 2025).

### Is the threat claim evidence-based?

No studies were found evidencing a link between foxes and the extinction of southern pig-footed bandicoots. All five bandicoot extirpation records pre-date fox arrival records.
<br>
<br>

![**Evidence linking *Chaeropus ecaudatus* to foxes.** Last records of extirpated populations relative to earliest local records of foxes. Error bars show record uncertainty range. Predator arrival records were digitized from Fairfax 2019.](assets/figures/Main_Evidence_Fox_Chaeropus ecaudatus.png)
